subject: General
notes: Format: ACCESS MODE IS {SEQUENTIAL|RANDOM|DYNAMIC}, ACCESS/SEQUENTIAL/RANDOM/DYNAMIC underlined, MODE and IS optional words (cite.py --check 12.4.5.5.1 "ACCESS" -> OK). Grammar accessModeClause : ACCESS MODE? IS? accessMode; accessMode : SEQUENTIAL|RANDOM|DYNAMIC -- exact match. DataBinder.BindFileControl maps it via MapAccessMode onto FileModel.AccessMode. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, --std 85 and 2023): 'ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC', 'ACCESS RANDOM', 'ACCESS IS DYNAMIC', 'ACCESS MODE SEQUENTIAL' all accepted and honoured (gA.cob, gB.cob); 'ACCESS MODE IS' with no mode rejected COBOL0312 (gE.cob); 'MODE IS RANDOM' without ACCESS rejected COBOL0312 (gF.cob). SIBLING (not this row): the FD grammar fileDescriptionClause (CobolData.g4:69-71) also admits organizationClause/accessModeClause/recordKeyClause, which §13.4.5.2's closed formats do not, and nothing reads them -- 'FD SQ ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC.' compiles and runs silently as a plain sequential file (gG.cob, gH.cob); reported as a finding against FMT-13.4.5.2. No spec-derived golden targets the clause's format variants, so test-ref is empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Annex E lists no substantive change to the ACCESS MODE clause)]
